# With -fp-reassoc, a loop that sums or multiplies floats is rewritten like an
# integer reduction, but the regrouped additions can round differently from the
# scalar loop, so it is opt-in. A float product feeding a sum is one multiply-add.
# The main loop folds four vectors per iteration into four accumulators so that
# the dependent adds overlap. The inputs here add exactly in any order, so the
# two builds print the same bits; the fuzz tests in bench/ check rounding.

# The scalar program is the reference behavior.
exec go run ./testmain
cmp stdout testmain/output

# Without the flag nothing is rewritten.
cp ops.go ops.go.orig
loopvec -split .
! stdout .
! stderr .
! exists ops_simd.go
cmp ops.go ops.go.orig

loopvec -fp-reassoc -split .
! stdout .
cmpenv stderr stderr.want
cmp ops_simd.go ops_simd.go.want
cmp ops.go ops.go.guarded

# The simd build must behave identically.
env GOEXPERIMENT=simd
exec go run ./testmain
cmp stdout testmain/output

-- go.mod --
module example.com/test

go 1.27.1
-- ops.go --
package test

func Sum(a []float32) float32 {
	var s float32
	for i := range a {
		s += a[i]
	}
	return s
}

// A product feeding a sum is one multiply-add.
func Dot(a, b []float64) float64 {
	var s float64
	for i, v := range a {
		s = s + v*b[i]
	}
	return s
}

func Product(a []float32) float32 {
	p := float32(1)
	for i := range a {
		p *= a[i]
	}
	return p
}

// Two folds in one loop, and an int limit.
func SumAndSquares(a []float64, n int) (float64, float64) {
	var s, q float64
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		s += a[i]
		q += a[i] * a[i]
	}
	return s, q
}

// Two folds, a temporary, and a range value variable: the shape of a weighted
// skewness.
func Moments(x, w []float64, mean, std float64) (s, sumWeights float64) {
	for i, v := range x {
		z := (v - mean) / std
		s += w[i] * z * z * z
		sumWeights += w[i]
	}
	return s, sumWeights
}
-- ops_simd.go.want --
//go:build goexperiment.simd

package test

import "simd"

func Sum(a []float32) float32 {
	var s float32
	{
		_i := 0
		if len(a) >= 64 {
			_a1_0 := simd.BroadcastFloat32s(0)
			_a1_1 := simd.BroadcastFloat32s(0)
			_a1_2 := simd.BroadcastFloat32s(0)
			_a1_3 := simd.BroadcastFloat32s(0)
			_lanes := _a1_0.Len()
			for ; _i+4*_lanes <= len(a); _i += 4 * _lanes {
				_v1 := simd.LoadFloat32s(a[_i:])
				_a1_0 = _a1_0.Add(_v1)
				_v2 := simd.LoadFloat32s(a[_i+_lanes:])
				_a1_1 = _a1_1.Add(_v2)
				_v3 := simd.LoadFloat32s(a[_i+2*_lanes:])
				_a1_2 = _a1_2.Add(_v3)
				_v4 := simd.LoadFloat32s(a[_i+3*_lanes:])
				_a1_3 = _a1_3.Add(_v4)
			}
			for ; _i+_lanes <= len(a); _i += _lanes {
				_v5 := simd.LoadFloat32s(a[_i:])
				_a1_0 = _a1_0.Add(_v5)
			}
			_a1_0 = _a1_0.Add(_a1_1)
			_a1_0 = _a1_0.Add(_a1_2)
			_a1_0 = _a1_0.Add(_a1_3)
			var _buf1 [16]float32
			_a1_0.Store(_buf1[:])
			for _, _x := range _buf1[:_lanes] {
				s = s + _x
			}
		}
		for i := _i; i < len(a); i++ {
			s += a[i]
		}
	}
	return s
}

// A product feeding a sum is one multiply-add.
func Dot(a, b []float64) float64 {
	var s float64
	if len(a) > 0 {
		_ = b[len(a)-1]
		{
			_i := 0
			if len(a) >= 32 {
				_a1_0 := simd.BroadcastFloat64s(0)
				_a1_1 := simd.BroadcastFloat64s(0)
				_a1_2 := simd.BroadcastFloat64s(0)
				_a1_3 := simd.BroadcastFloat64s(0)
				_lanes := _a1_0.Len()
				for ; _i+4*_lanes <= len(a); _i += 4 * _lanes {
					_v1 := simd.LoadFloat64s(a[_i:])
					_v2 := simd.LoadFloat64s(b[_i:])
					_a1_0 = _v1.MulAdd(_v2, _a1_0)
					_v3 := simd.LoadFloat64s(a[_i+_lanes:])
					_v4 := simd.LoadFloat64s(b[_i+_lanes:])
					_a1_1 = _v3.MulAdd(_v4, _a1_1)
					_v5 := simd.LoadFloat64s(a[_i+2*_lanes:])
					_v6 := simd.LoadFloat64s(b[_i+2*_lanes:])
					_a1_2 = _v5.MulAdd(_v6, _a1_2)
					_v7 := simd.LoadFloat64s(a[_i+3*_lanes:])
					_v8 := simd.LoadFloat64s(b[_i+3*_lanes:])
					_a1_3 = _v7.MulAdd(_v8, _a1_3)
				}
				for ; _i+_lanes <= len(a); _i += _lanes {
					_v9 := simd.LoadFloat64s(a[_i:])
					_v10 := simd.LoadFloat64s(b[_i:])
					_a1_0 = _v9.MulAdd(_v10, _a1_0)
				}
				_a1_0 = _a1_0.Add(_a1_1)
				_a1_0 = _a1_0.Add(_a1_2)
				_a1_0 = _a1_0.Add(_a1_3)
				var _buf1 [8]float64
				_a1_0.Store(_buf1[:])
				for _, _x := range _buf1[:_lanes] {
					s = s + _x
				}
			}
			for i := _i; i < len(a); i++ {
				v := a[i]
				s = s + v*b[i]
			}
		}
	}
	return s
}

func Product(a []float32) float32 {
	p := float32(1)
	{
		_i := 0
		if len(a) >= 64 {
			_a1_0 := simd.BroadcastFloat32s(1)
			_a1_1 := simd.BroadcastFloat32s(1)
			_a1_2 := simd.BroadcastFloat32s(1)
			_a1_3 := simd.BroadcastFloat32s(1)
			_lanes := _a1_0.Len()
			for ; _i+4*_lanes <= len(a); _i += 4 * _lanes {
				_v1 := simd.LoadFloat32s(a[_i:])
				_a1_0 = _a1_0.Mul(_v1)
				_v2 := simd.LoadFloat32s(a[_i+_lanes:])
				_a1_1 = _a1_1.Mul(_v2)
				_v3 := simd.LoadFloat32s(a[_i+2*_lanes:])
				_a1_2 = _a1_2.Mul(_v3)
				_v4 := simd.LoadFloat32s(a[_i+3*_lanes:])
				_a1_3 = _a1_3.Mul(_v4)
			}
			for ; _i+_lanes <= len(a); _i += _lanes {
				_v5 := simd.LoadFloat32s(a[_i:])
				_a1_0 = _a1_0.Mul(_v5)
			}
			_a1_0 = _a1_0.Mul(_a1_1)
			_a1_0 = _a1_0.Mul(_a1_2)
			_a1_0 = _a1_0.Mul(_a1_3)
			var _buf1 [16]float32
			_a1_0.Store(_buf1[:])
			for _, _x := range _buf1[:_lanes] {
				p = p * _x
			}
		}
		for i := _i; i < len(a); i++ {
			p *= a[i]
		}
	}
	return p
}

// Two folds in one loop, and an int limit.
func SumAndSquares(a []float64, n int) (float64, float64) {
	var s, q float64
	if n > 0 {
		_ = a[n-1]
		{
			_i := 0
			if n >= 32 {
				_a1_0 := simd.BroadcastFloat64s(0)
				_a1_1 := simd.BroadcastFloat64s(0)
				_a1_2 := simd.BroadcastFloat64s(0)
				_a1_3 := simd.BroadcastFloat64s(0)
				_a2_0 := simd.BroadcastFloat64s(0)
				_a2_1 := simd.BroadcastFloat64s(0)
				_a2_2 := simd.BroadcastFloat64s(0)
				_a2_3 := simd.BroadcastFloat64s(0)
				_lanes := _a1_0.Len()
				for ; _i+4*_lanes <= n; _i += 4 * _lanes {
					_v1 := simd.LoadFloat64s(a[_i:])
					_a1_0 = _a1_0.Add(_v1)
					_a2_0 = _v1.MulAdd(_v1, _a2_0)
					_v2 := simd.LoadFloat64s(a[_i+_lanes:])
					_a1_1 = _a1_1.Add(_v2)
					_a2_1 = _v2.MulAdd(_v2, _a2_1)
					_v3 := simd.LoadFloat64s(a[_i+2*_lanes:])
					_a1_2 = _a1_2.Add(_v3)
					_a2_2 = _v3.MulAdd(_v3, _a2_2)
					_v4 := simd.LoadFloat64s(a[_i+3*_lanes:])
					_a1_3 = _a1_3.Add(_v4)
					_a2_3 = _v4.MulAdd(_v4, _a2_3)
				}
				for ; _i+_lanes <= n; _i += _lanes {
					_v5 := simd.LoadFloat64s(a[_i:])
					_a1_0 = _a1_0.Add(_v5)
					_a2_0 = _v5.MulAdd(_v5, _a2_0)
				}
				_a1_0 = _a1_0.Add(_a1_1)
				_a1_0 = _a1_0.Add(_a1_2)
				_a1_0 = _a1_0.Add(_a1_3)
				var _buf1 [8]float64
				_a1_0.Store(_buf1[:])
				for _, _x := range _buf1[:_lanes] {
					s = s + _x
				}
				_a2_0 = _a2_0.Add(_a2_1)
				_a2_0 = _a2_0.Add(_a2_2)
				_a2_0 = _a2_0.Add(_a2_3)
				var _buf2 [8]float64
				_a2_0.Store(_buf2[:])
				for _, _x := range _buf2[:_lanes] {
					q = q + _x
				}
			}
			for i := _i; i < n; i++ {
				s += a[i]
				q += a[i] * a[i]
			}
		}
	}
	return s, q
}

// Two folds, a temporary, and a range value variable: the shape of a weighted
// skewness.
func Moments(x, w []float64, mean, std float64) (s, sumWeights float64) {
	_vcFloat64s4_1 := simd.BroadcastFloat64s(mean)
	_vcFloat64s4_2 := simd.BroadcastFloat64s(std)
	if len(x) > 0 {
		_ = w[len(x)-1]
		{
			_i := 0
			if len(x) >= 32 {
				_a1_0 := simd.BroadcastFloat64s(0)
				_a1_1 := simd.BroadcastFloat64s(0)
				_a1_2 := simd.BroadcastFloat64s(0)
				_a1_3 := simd.BroadcastFloat64s(0)
				_a2_0 := simd.BroadcastFloat64s(0)
				_a2_1 := simd.BroadcastFloat64s(0)
				_a2_2 := simd.BroadcastFloat64s(0)
				_a2_3 := simd.BroadcastFloat64s(0)
				_lanes := _a1_0.Len()
				for ; _i+4*_lanes <= len(x); _i += 4 * _lanes {
					_v1 := simd.LoadFloat64s(x[_i:])
					_t1 := _v1.Sub(_vcFloat64s4_1).Div(_vcFloat64s4_2)
					_v2 := simd.LoadFloat64s(w[_i:])
					_a1_0 = _v2.Mul(_t1).Mul(_t1).MulAdd(_t1, _a1_0)
					_a2_0 = _a2_0.Add(_v2)
					_v3 := simd.LoadFloat64s(x[_i+_lanes:])
					_t2 := _v3.Sub(_vcFloat64s4_1).Div(_vcFloat64s4_2)
					_v4 := simd.LoadFloat64s(w[_i+_lanes:])
					_a1_1 = _v4.Mul(_t2).Mul(_t2).MulAdd(_t2, _a1_1)
					_a2_1 = _a2_1.Add(_v4)
					_v5 := simd.LoadFloat64s(x[_i+2*_lanes:])
					_t3 := _v5.Sub(_vcFloat64s4_1).Div(_vcFloat64s4_2)
					_v6 := simd.LoadFloat64s(w[_i+2*_lanes:])
					_a1_2 = _v6.Mul(_t3).Mul(_t3).MulAdd(_t3, _a1_2)
					_a2_2 = _a2_2.Add(_v6)
					_v7 := simd.LoadFloat64s(x[_i+3*_lanes:])
					_t4 := _v7.Sub(_vcFloat64s4_1).Div(_vcFloat64s4_2)
					_v8 := simd.LoadFloat64s(w[_i+3*_lanes:])
					_a1_3 = _v8.Mul(_t4).Mul(_t4).MulAdd(_t4, _a1_3)
					_a2_3 = _a2_3.Add(_v8)
				}
				for ; _i+_lanes <= len(x); _i += _lanes {
					_v9 := simd.LoadFloat64s(x[_i:])
					_t5 := _v9.Sub(_vcFloat64s4_1).Div(_vcFloat64s4_2)
					_v10 := simd.LoadFloat64s(w[_i:])
					_a1_0 = _v10.Mul(_t5).Mul(_t5).MulAdd(_t5, _a1_0)
					_a2_0 = _a2_0.Add(_v10)
				}
				_a1_0 = _a1_0.Add(_a1_1)
				_a1_0 = _a1_0.Add(_a1_2)
				_a1_0 = _a1_0.Add(_a1_3)
				var _buf1 [8]float64
				_a1_0.Store(_buf1[:])
				for _, _x := range _buf1[:_lanes] {
					s = s + _x
				}
				_a2_0 = _a2_0.Add(_a2_1)
				_a2_0 = _a2_0.Add(_a2_2)
				_a2_0 = _a2_0.Add(_a2_3)
				var _buf2 [8]float64
				_a2_0.Store(_buf2[:])
				for _, _x := range _buf2[:_lanes] {
					sumWeights = sumWeights + _x
				}
			}
			for i := _i; i < len(x); i++ {
				v := x[i]
				z := (v - mean) / std
				s += w[i] * z * z * z
				sumWeights += w[i]
			}
		}
	}
	return s, sumWeights
}
-- testmain/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"math"

	"example.com/test"
)

// The sizes cover empty, shorter than a vector, one vector, the unrolled loop
// and its tail.
var sizes = []int{0, 1, 2, 7, 8, 9, 15, 16, 17, 31, 32, 33, 63, 64, 65, 100, 127, 128, 129, 200, 256, 257, 1000}

func main() {
	// Small integers and powers of two add and multiply exactly in any order, so
	// the regrouped loop gives the same bits as the scalar one.
	for _, n := range sizes {
		a32 := make([]float32, n)
		p32 := make([]float32, n)
		a64 := make([]float64, n)
		b64 := make([]float64, n)
		for i := range n {
			a32[i] = float32(i%97 - 40)
			p32[i] = [3]float32{1, 2, 0.5}[i%3]
			a64[i], b64[i] = float64(i%61-30), float64(i%13)
		}
		s, q := test.SumAndSquares(a64, n)
		m, w := test.Moments(a64, b64, 3, 1)
		fmt.Println(n, test.Sum(a32), test.Dot(a64, b64), test.Product(p32), s, q, m, w)
	}

	// A NaN or an infinity in any position gives the same answer in any order.
	for _, n := range []int{5, 70, 300} {
		a := make([]float32, n)
		for i := range a {
			a[i] = 1
		}
		a[n/2] = float32(math.NaN())
		fmt.Println(n, test.Sum(a))
		a[n/2] = float32(math.Inf(1))
		fmt.Println(n, test.Sum(a))
		a[n-1] = float32(math.Inf(-1))
		fmt.Println(n, test.Sum(a))
	}
}

-- ops.go.guarded --
//go:build !goexperiment.simd

package test

func Sum(a []float32) float32 {
	var s float32
	for i := range a {
		s += a[i]
	}
	return s
}

// A product feeding a sum is one multiply-add.
func Dot(a, b []float64) float64 {
	var s float64
	for i, v := range a {
		s = s + v*b[i]
	}
	return s
}

func Product(a []float32) float32 {
	p := float32(1)
	for i := range a {
		p *= a[i]
	}
	return p
}

// Two folds in one loop, and an int limit.
func SumAndSquares(a []float64, n int) (float64, float64) {
	var s, q float64
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		s += a[i]
		q += a[i] * a[i]
	}
	return s, q
}

// Two folds, a temporary, and a range value variable: the shape of a weighted
// skewness.
func Moments(x, w []float64, mean, std float64) (s, sumWeights float64) {
	for i, v := range x {
		z := (v - mean) / std
		s += w[i] * z * z * z
		sumWeights += w[i]
	}
	return s, sumWeights
}
